John Ternus officially takes over as Apple’s CEO today, and as Myke Hurley pointed out, his new personal profile page on Apple’s official website reveals some of his main work priorities.

John Ternus’s new Apple bio, on his first day as CEO, has revealed his work priorities

Apple today updated its leadership page to change John Ternus’s title to CEO.

In addition to updating the leadership information, Ternus’s official bio was also updated and expanded.

As Myke Hurley pointed out in The Enthusiast, the new bio emphasises Ternus’s career at Apple and three key areas he deeply values. Two of these areas are brand new.

Although part of the bio retains previous content, there is one entirely new paragraph. Quoted below, the content comes from Apple’s official website:

This is the only entirely new paragraph. The rest of the bio is either the same as before, or only slightly reworded, with the core message unchanged.

This new paragraph takes up nearly half of the entire bio, and the bio itself is fairly short.

Therefore, this paragraph alone clearly shows the priorities that Ternus greatly values and wants to emphasise at the start of his tenure as CEO.

The key points of this paragraph can be summarised as: Ternus values hardware "reliability and durability," as well as "innovation in materials and hardware design," with the goal of reducing carbon footprint and extending product lifespan.

We’ve all seen Tim Cook consistently pushing hard to reduce Apple’s carbon footprint. Ternus is clearly signalling that this direction will continue under his leadership. But this paragraph also emphasises that Ternus himself is an innovator in hardware design, committed to making products that can last for many years.

What do you think of John Ternus’s new CEO bio? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
